edges.rationale: SampleRTT is measured by timing the transmission of a segment and receipt of its acknowledgment, which requires understanding sequence/acknowledgment numbers and the ACK flag defined in the segment structure.

Reliable data transfer is built on the 32-bit sequence and acknowledgment numbers (byte-stream offsets) and the ACK flag; cumulative acknowledgments cannot be understood without the segment's numbering scheme.
Flow control relies on the receive window (rwnd) field carried in the TCP segment header; the sender reads this field to limit unacknowledged data.
The three-way handshake and teardown use the SYN, FIN, ACK, and RST header flags and involve sequence number selection, all defined in the segment structure.
The single retransmission timer's behavior, including timeout-triggered retransmissions and doubling the timeout, directly uses the TimeoutInterval computed from EstimatedRTT and DevRTT.
Flow control constrains the amount of unacknowledged (in-flight) data, a concept defined by the sender's acknowledgment and windowing behavior in reliable data transfer (LastByteSent, LastByteAcked).
Connection management details the lifecycle (handshake, state, teardown) of the connection abstraction; understanding why a handshake and per-connection state exist must come first.
